primitives.name: Nested Zero-Inflated Generalized Poisson Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes a *nested* zero-inflated generalized Poisson (ZIGP) regression that models the stronger team's goals from both attack and defense perspectives (averaged), then models the weaker team's goals *conditional on* the stronger team's realized score — and validates it against classical Poisson models on five past tournaments.
primitives.latex:
\begin{aligned}
&\text{For team } A \text{ (stronger by Elo):} \\
&\quad \log \mu_A(\text{Elo}_B) = \alpha_0^{(1)} + \alpha_1^{(1)} \text{Elo}_B + \alpha_2^{(1)} \text{loc}; \quad \phi_A = 1 + e^{\beta^{(1)}}; \quad \omega_A = \frac{\gamma^{(1)}}{1 + \gamma^{(1)}} \\
&\text{For team } B \text{ (weaker):} \\
&\quad \log \nu_B(\text{Elo}_A) = \alpha_0^{(2)} + \alpha_1^{(2)} \text{Elo}_A + \alpha_2^{(2)} \text{loc}; \quad \psi_B, \delta_B \text{ analogous} \\
&\text{Average parameters: } (\mu_{A|B}, \phi_{A|B}, \omega_{A|B}) \\
&\text{Conditional on } G_A: \log \bar{\mu}_{B|A} = \alpha_0^{(3)} + \alpha_1^{(3)} \text{Elo}_A + \alpha_2^{(3)} \text{loc} + \alpha_3^{(3)} G_A
\end{aligned}

primitives.name: Elo Rating Update Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Elo update: Elo_after = Elo_before + K·G·(W-W_e); W_e = 1/(10^{-D/400}+1), D = Elo diff; G = 1 (draw/1-goal win), 1.5 (2-goal win), (11+N)/8 otherwise; K=60 (WC), 50 (continental), etc.

reasoning_traces.think:
The nested ZIGP regression operates by decomposing team scoring into attack and defense components, modeling the stronger team’s goals first using a ZIGP distribution based on opponent Elo and match location. Then, the weaker team’s goals are modeled conditionally on the stronger team’s realized score, capturing a 'defensive relaxation' effect. This nested structure allows for more nuanced modeling of low-count, overdispersed, and zero-inflated goal data. The model uses log-linear link functions with parameters estimated via maximum likelihood. The inclusion of date and importance weights ensures that recent and significant matches contribute more heavily to the model fit. In GSE, this translates to a hierarchical simulation engine where team strengths are updated dynamically based on simulated outcomes, leveraging the same nested structure to predict playoff progression and championship probabilities. The Elo update mechanism provides a feedback loop for team strength recalibration within each simulation, ensuring realistic temporal dynamics. The date and importance weighting further refine the historical data used for fitting, aligning with GSE’s emphasis on form and context-sensitive modeling.
